title: The 'Cancel Anytime' Trap Is Stealing $1,200 From You
hook: That button promised 'cancel anytime' — companies deliberately hide the cancel option 7 screens deep so you give up and keep paying. The FTC documented $1.2 billion in consumer harm from this one trick.
angle: Exposes the deliberate UX dark pattern that traps subscribers — moving from psychology to FTC enforcement data to the personal cost math, then the simple bank-statement fix
audience: Anyone 18-45 with streaming, app, gym, or software subscriptions
key_numbers: FTC documented $1.2B in consumer harm from subscription dark patterns (2023)
Hard-cancel designs keep 15% more users who wanted to leave
Average person has 4 forgotten subscriptions at $25/month each
40% of people give up trying to cancel mid-attempt
